title: Happychess devastation
transcript: Not every beautiful and crazy combination is played by a grandmaster. This game was sent to me by my friend Happy Chess and it's a game that he played against Afid the master on chess.com in a blitz game. In this position, black plays E5 now attacking the bishop. And after trading once, we have to move the bishop or we're going to lose it, right? Well, not exactly. Happy Chess plays rook D to G1. The first of four brilliant moves in this sequence. Now, of course, black takes the free bishop. And it seems like everything here is well defended by the knight, bishop, and queen, but it's all an illusion. And here comes the first rook sacrifice. Rook takes G4. And now that the bishop is not covering H5 anymore, the knight cannot capture because otherwise this rook check would pick up the queen and this would be an easy win for white. So instead, the opponent takes in the center one more time. After all, he's won a bishop. So he doesn't mind losing a bishop of his own. And now he's attacking a knight. But white doesn't care for the knight and he plays bishop takes H5. Now setting up a discover attack. if it wasn't for the fact that this bishop is simply hanging and indeed it gets captured. But now white follows up with rook to G5 now attacking the queen and the knight at the same time. Black is [music] left with nothing better but to sacrifice the queen. But after this move, white is threatening checkmate in one move. So black has to defend before picking up this knight. Now of course the knight can move away. Except it doesn't. And happy chess sacrifices the other rook. The rook cannot be taken otherwise this would be a checkmate. The king has to move and only a few moves later defeat a master opponent had to resign in this position because the game is completely lost. What a beautiful sequence. And if you love sacrificial chess like this, I suggest you check out his page, Happy Chess Official.
